title: AERO9500 Report Marking Rubric (Assignment Part 2)

criteria.name:
Introduction: mission concept and rationale
- Include the following required information:
• What is the spacecraft's primary mission?
• Why is the mission needed?
• How many spacecraft are used and why?
• Who are the users (operator and customers)?

levels.label: Accomplished 7–10 marks
levels.desc: Addresses all requirements to a high standard. Detailed descriptions and discussions are included. References to literature as appropriate.

levels.label: Adequate 4–6 marks
levels.desc: Addresses some requirements. Descriptions may feature lack of specific details and/or incomplete referencing.

levels.label: Deficient 0–3 marks
levels.desc: Many or all requirements are not addressed. Poor descriptions or lack of appropriate referencing.

criteria.name:
Main body: mission design
- Present a summary of the mission design using software and/or hand calculations as appropriate
- Include relevant screenshots and software files (in the main body of the report and/or appendix)
- Include the following information:
• Where it will launch from, and using which launch vehicle? Why did you choose this option?
• What type of orbit will you use? What are its characteristics and orbital elements?
• Will you need to perform any orbital maneuvers?
• Which ground control facilities will you use?
• How often will your spacecraft be able to communicate with ground control?
• How long will the mission last, and what are your plans for EOL?

levels.label: Accomplished 7–10 marks
levels.desc: Demonstrates high level understanding of the design procedure. Design clearly addresses mission and course concepts. Major requirements are all addressed and are well supported with quality evidence (eg. software screenshots, software files, hand calculations, references from literature). Content is comprehensive, accurate, and persuasive.

levels.label: Adequate 4–6 marks
levels.desc: Demonstrates adequate understanding of the design procedure. Design may be inconsistent with regards to purpose and clarity of thought or feature errors. Major requirements are addressed but may lack some detail or are not well supported with evidence. Content may not be comprehensive and/or persuasive.

levels.label: Deficient 0–3 marks
levels.desc: Demonstrates minimal understanding of the design procedure. Major requirements are not addressed and/or lack evidence. Content is incomplete or not persuasive.

levels.label: Accomplished 7–10 marks
levels.desc: Detailed and appropriate conclusions reached from the evidence provided in the report.

levels.label: Adequate 4–6 marks
levels.desc: Some conclusions are reached but they may be generic or lack specific detail.

levels.label: Deficient 0–3 marks
levels.desc: No actual or useful conclusions reached.

levels.label: Accomplished 7–10 marks
levels.desc: The document follows a clear and logical engineering report structure. The report is easy to read: well-written, with good spelling and grammar, and appropriate language style. All aspects of formatting are consistent throughout the document. Executive summary (or abstract) provides a concise overview of the report. Graphical and tabular presentation of data is appropriate, clear and consistent. References in text match reference list (and vice versa) and are cited properly.

levels.label: Adequate 4–6 marks
levels.desc: Document is not at a professional level but does make use of headings and subheadings to indicate document structure. The report may be difficult to read: writing is just ok, broad idea comes across; spelling and grammar have some flaws, not quite appropriate language style. Although figures and tables are labelled, the formatting is unclear and/or inconsistent to the extent that the reader can lose track of the context when reading. References in text match reference list (and vice versa) and are mostly cited correctly.

levels.label: Deficient 0–3 marks
levels.desc: The document is poorly structured, is not coherent or shows a lack of understanding of the purpose of its sections. Much effort is required to read and understand the report: writing is poor, many mistakes with spelling and grammar, and possibly inappropriate language style (e.g. too informal). Presentation is poor to the extent that it impedes reading of the document. Examples include inconsistent formatting, and unlabelled figures or tables. References are either not cited or cited inconsistently.

notes: 25% of course grade. Performance levels use a common 7–10 / 4–6 / 0–3 mark scale for each criterion. No total marks or per-criterion maximum marks are printed.
